   (1) Adopt the Environmental Determination that the proposed

  The City Clerk reported that 79 letters were received in opposition
  to the proposed project, 4 letters received in favor of the proposed
  project and 3 letters providing comments were received by the City
  Clerk's office, which were distributed to the City Council, posted
  online, and made part of the public hearing record.

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community DeVelopment,
  and Jason Van Patten, Associate Planner, provided a PowerPoint
  presentation on the item, reviewed amendments to Ccmditions of
  Approval Nos. 100, 101 , and 102, and jointly, responded to
  questions.

D  The following individuals (appellants) expressed concerns with
  . the Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) to approve Affordable Housing

  applicant in submitting a revised project:

  Sue Mossman, Pasadena Heritage
  Annie Perez, Women's City Club
  Bill Ellinger, Blinn House Foundation
  Andrew Salimian, Pasadena Heritage

  Richard A. McDonald , representing the applicant, spoke on the
  work done by the Applicant's development team to build
  consensus (i.e. meeting with Pasadena Heritage and other
  representatives of the appellants), and spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation .

  The following individuals provided comment on the item:

  Nina Chomsky, Pasadena resident
  Emily Murray, representing Allen Matkins (distributed

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke in . favor of the staff
  recommendation and asked staff to consider amending a
  Condition of Approval that will address the tree canopy issues
  shared by surrounding property owners.

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's request to add~ess the
  tree canopy, Jennifer Paige, Deputy Director of Planning, stated
  that staff recommends amending Condition of Approval No. 93 to
  include the following sentence, "The plan shall also consider
  protected trees on adjacent properties to ensure they continue to
  survive .post-construction."

  The City Council thanked the community, appellants, and
  applicant/developers for working together to develop a project that
  is acceptable to all parties involved .

  Vice Mayor Hampton stated his appreciation for the consensus
  building performed as part of this project, and suggested that such

D  steps be taken by developers with the community for similar
  projects proposed within the City. He spoke in favor of agendizing
  a general discussion on California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) process; and ensure projects include a description of all
  environmental impacts on surrounding neighborhoods/areas. He
  also reiterated his request to agendize a review of the City's
  General Plan at a future City Council meeting.

  In response to Vice Mayor Hampton's request, Mayor Tornek
  stated that staff and the Legislative Policy Committee are waiting
  to learn the status of new state-sponsored legislation, which will
  require staff to analyze the impacts of the new legislation, with
  staff to return to the City Council with an update.

  Councilmember Wilson requested that staff review the City's
  traffic model to ensure it is updated with current state legislation;
  and expressed concerns with weaknesses in the City's current
  tree protection ordinance that does not protect mature trees. He
  asked staff to review the ordinance and consider proposing
  additional tree protections, as well as provisions that would be
  more restrictive on tree replacement practices for development
  projects.

  thresholds, setbacks, and open space requirements.
